column2: I have taken hold of the wisdom of truth from my father; I have been born like the sun.
May our rich cattle, strong in vigor, be with Indra in the shared feast, by which we may rejoice with plenty.
Soma and Pushan awaken to all the good dwellings; among the gods they are placed for the charioteers.
Sing to Indra, the best protector of your drink — the all-conquering, hundred-powered, greatest of the peoples.
Sing the exhilarating song for Indra of the bay horses, friends — for the drinker of soma.
We, O Indra, longing for you, friends with this very aim, the Kanvas, praise you with hymns.
Let our songs resound around Indra for the pressed exhilarating soma; let the singers sing the hymn.
This soma of yours, O Indra, is purified on the grass; come, hasten and drink it.
For help we invoke day by day him who makes fair forms, like a good milker for the one who milks.
O bull, I pour out the pressed soma for you to drink; be satisfied and attain exhilaration.
O Indra, the soma pressed for you in the cups and vessels — you are lord of it; drink it.
At every yoking, at every battle, we, friends, invoke Indra, the mightiest, for help.
Come and sit down; sing to Indra, friends who bear the hymn.
This has been pressed with strength, O lord of bounties; drink of it, you who love songs.
Great is Indra, and may greatness be before us for the thunderbolt-bearer; his strength spreads wide like heaven.
Now, Indra, take hold of the abundant, wondrous grasp for us, great-handed, with your right hand.
Praise with song Indra, lord of cattle, as one who knows — son of truth, lord of the good.
By what wondrous help shall he come to us, an ever-growing friend? By what mighty company?
We praise him, who is conqueror in all battles, stretched out in all songs; may you bring him to help us.
I have sought the wise, the lord of the assembly, wondrous, dear to Indra, desirable — a gift of insight.
The paths of yours which lie below heaven, by which you drove the horseless — may the lands also hear us.
Bring us every good thing, strength and food, O hundred-powered; since, Indra, you make us happy.
This soma has been pressed; the Maruts drink of it, and also the self-ruling Ashvins.
The waters, busy and moving, wait on the newborn Indra, desiring heroic strength.
We do not harm the gods, nor do we bring them to harm; we walk by the hearing of the mantra.
Evening has come; sing the great, the radiant song, O Atharvan descendant; praise the god Savitar.
This incomparable Dawn dawns, the beloved of heaven; I praise you, Ashvins, loudly.
Indra, with the bones of Dadhyanch, unresisted, slew the Vritras, ninety-nine times.
Come, Indra, rejoice in the drink, with all the soma-joints; great is your aim, great your strength.
Come to us now, Indra, Vritra-slayer, to our sacrifice, great one, with great helps.
His strength shone forth when he turned both worlds like a skin, Indra, heaven and earth.
Here for you, in the contest, like a dove to its nest — you carry that word of ours as well.
O wind, blow healing; bring comfort and joy to our hearts, and extend our lives.
The man whom the wise Varuna, Mitra and Aryaman protect — no one harms him.
Desiring cattle, and horses and chariots, as before, do homage to the great ones.
These dappled cows of yours, Indra, yield the ghee-mixed drink, swelling with this of truth.
By this thought, desiring cattle, O much-named, much-praised, whenever you are present at every soma.
May the purifying Sarasvati, rich in strength, with strengths, desire our sacrifice, she who gives wealth through thought.
Who will satisfy this Indra among the human clans with soma? May he bring us treasures.
Come, for we have pressed for you, Indra; drink this soma; come to this grass, my seat.
May the great, heaven-dwelling, indomitable protection of the three — Mitra, Aryaman, Varuna — be below us.
We are of those like you, O rich in wealth, O leader, Indra; stand, lord of the bay horses.
May the soma-drops delight you; make us rich, O stone-bearer; strike down the haters of prayer.
O you who love songs, protect our pressed soma; you are anointed with streams of honey; Indra, fame is what you have given.
Indra ever does good for you; he will worship near; the hero Indra is not a god who is resisted.
May the drops enter you as rivers the sea; none excels you, Indra.
The singers sing to Indra great songs; those with hymns, with hymns; the voices praised Indra.
May Indra give us food, wealth, skilled and bright; may the strong one give the strong.
Indra, indeed, has driven away great fear; he is steady and all-seeing.
These songs of ours, O lover of songs, reach you at every pressing, like cows reaching their calf.
Now Indra and Pushan, we call on you for friendship, for welfare, for the winning of strength.
Nothing, Indra, is higher than you, nothing greater, Vritra-slayer; none is such as you.
I praise the same one for you: the deliverer of the peoples, the giver of strength with cattle.
Our songs have gone out to you, Indra; they rise to you, the bull, the lord, in harmony.
He is indeed the well-led mortal whom the Maruts and Aryaman, the friends, guard without deceit.
Whatever wealth is hidden in strength, in steadiness, or in the far distance — bring that desirable wealth.
The famed best Vritra-slayer, the force of the peoples, is for blessing and great bounty.
May we reach enough fame for you, O hero Indra; enough, powerful one, in the far attack.
Indra, enjoy this morning our offering of roasted grain, porridge, cakes and hymns.
With the foam of the waters, Indra, you cut off the head of Namuchi, when you conquered all rivals.
These soma-drops are yours, Indra, those pressed and those yet to be pressed; rejoice in them, O lord of wealth.
The pressed somas are for you, the grass is spread, O shining one; be gracious to the singers, Indra.
O Indra, hundred-powered like a skilled worker, desiring strength, I pour the greatest soma-drops for you.
From here, Indra, come to us with a hundred strengths, with food that brings a thousand strengths.
The Vritra-slayer took the arrow; born, he asked his mother: who are the mighty, who are heard of?
We call on the one of great hymns, the shining-handed, for help — one who accomplishes for protection.
May Varuna, Mitra, knowing, lead us by the straight path, and Aryaman in harmony with the gods.
When from afar, as if here, the ruddy-limbed one blazed, he spread his light everywhere.
O Mitra and Varuna, skilled ones, sprinkle our pasture with ghee and our realms with honey.
These sons of ours have stretched the songs to the goal at the sacrifices, to go forth with eager spirits.
Vishnu strode across this; he set his foot in three ways; the whole was gathered in his dusty step.
Pass by the one who is full of wrath; urge on the one who has pressed; drink the pressed soma in his gift.
What word is spoken to the great wise god? That alone increases him.
Neither the recited hymn nor the wealth is known to be praised; nor is the Gayatri sung.
Indra is the most exhilarating with hymns and lord of strengths; he has bay horses and is friend of the pressed soma.
Come to our pressed soma with your strengths; do not be angry at us, like a great young husband.
When, O Vasu, will the praise reach him, the beloved, and hold back the strongly spread hostility? The long pressing for the wind to swell.
O Indra, drink soma from the Brahmin's offering, following the seasons; this friendship of yours is unconquered.
We too are yours, Indra, your praisers, lover of songs; you, soma-drinker, quicken us.
Come, Indra, place manly vigor in our bodies in all the battles; O ever-victorious, mighty one, give us strength.
So indeed you are hero-loving, so indeed brave and steady; so your mind is to be won.
We cry to you, O hero, like unmilked cows — you who rule this world, who see the sun, who rule what stands, Indra.
We call on you alone for the winning of strength, the poets; you, lord of the good in battles, Indra — men call on you, as do racers at the goals.
Praise Indra, bounteous, as one who knows, who gives to singers, rich in wealth, giving as if by thousands.
Him, your wondrous victor over foes, rejoicing in the soma-drink of the Vasu — with songs we praise Indra anew, as cows their calf in their stalls.
With strengths I invoke Indra, finder of wealth, together with our fellows for help, at the soma-pressing sacrifice, singing loudly, as one calls a worker for his burden.
The swift one desires strength with his yoked fullness; with song I bow to Indra, invoked by many, as a carpenter to a well-running wheel-rim.
Drink the flavored pressed soma, Indra, and rejoice for us, rich in cattle; be our kinsman in the shared feast; may your thoughts protect us.
You come, for the wanderer; find fortune for the winning of wealth; rise up, bounteous one, for the seeking of cattle, Indra, for the seeking of horses.
For neither the last nor Vasishtha will be shut out from you; today, O Maruts, may all the wishful ones drink together at our pressing.
